content:
The image shows a severely desiccated, brown, curled/twisted leaf — completely dried out with uniform brown coloration and no green tissue remaining. The leaf has curled lengthwise into a tube-like shape.

Key observations:
- Entire leaf is uniformly brown/dead
- Leaf is severely curled/twisted along its length
- No spots, lesions, powdery coating, or fungal structures visible
- This pattern of shoot/leaf dieback with complete desiccation is characteristic of **Die Back** disease, where terminal shoots and leaves die and dry out completely

This matches Die Back, not:
- Anthracnose (would show dark lesions/spots)
- Bacterial Canker (would show canker lesions on stem/bark)
- Cutting Weevil (would show physical cuts/notches)
- Gall Midge (would show galls/swellings)
- Powdery Mildew (would show white powdery coating)
- Sooty Mould (would show black sooty coating)
